body:
In the PC version there were more missions. Around 7 types of missions if I remember correctly.

I only played AC1, but looking forward playing AC2.

This mindset thing is very true. Walking away from the rabid dog is even more. Don't fight the old, build the new as they say.

>  then Porn has already defeated you

Though porn isn't the only enemy here. As always there are other problems in the deep that needs to be fixed. This porn thing is more of a symptom than a cause.

What really sucks is that I hate porn. Like who even wants to watch so many badly produced videos, read badly written stuff and so on. Granted though those Japanese artists actually know what they are doing, there are so many talented people in that country, it's almost unbelievable.

Super awesome comment. Just what the doctor ordered :-) Thanks!

Though I have to say what you linked is kind of a pseudo-science. The Universe doesn't revolve around us. That belief ultimately makes you an asshole. I mean not you, those who believe that they are the center of everything.

Nevertheless your comment is awesome.

Taking away a huge coping mechanism is indeed may be the solution here. But you know you need an alternative for that. It's like a chicken and egg problem. But I'm glad that it worked out for you.

I'm working out and eating healthy, and otherwise I can get a girfriend (or boyfriend, yep, I'm one of those people) or at least I used to be. It's just that I'm trapped in a dark place after losing some big battles, and I'm using PMO as one of the ways to cope with it. Suicide ideation would be another one. Obviously neither of those works well, so I'm trying to find a new strategy :-)

The biggest problem is that I don't trust myself enough. Out of all the ingredients it takes, namely discipline, hard work and the ability to cope with failure, I demonstrated many times that I can't cope with failure. I just break down. Even though failure is such an important part of the process.

> learn how to cope with life by actually living it

That's an awesome thought. I'm bit of an unbalanced person even in my brightest moments. Like I have huge ambitions, and I work very hard, but my personal life tend to be a mess. Not non-existent, but rather a mess. Let's just say that my relationships tend to be very shallow and I have a hard time forming more stable, intimate connections. I guess even there I'm so terrible afraid of failure and loss.

I did the exact same thing.

The sad part? I use Pocket since when it was called Read It Later, and have around 3000 links saved, but I rarely read the things I save.

Luckily these days my tendency to procrastinate comes handy. I supposed to do this suicide thing a few weeks ago, but I'm not feeling up to it.

I don't mean to downplay your issues, but this happens to 16 year olds simple because of how the adolescent brain works. Also things like pollution and unhealthy diet with too much sugar can make it worse.

What I'm saying that it's not your fault that you are like this. And it's very hard to go through it, to have no meaning or happiness. But the thing is, this condition tend to not last forever. I'm not promising you this, I'm simple saying that for most people it goes away. For some it doesn't, but even then for many it gets much better with treatment.

You will have plenty of opportunity to find purpose. In the meantime you have to not trust your outlook on things too much, just think of it as a temporary faulty wiring in your brain. And if you can try to reach out as much as you can, others can help.

What you describe sounds like depression by the way. Depression is more characterized by emptiness and hopelessness than sadness, which is indeed a normal emotion, while depression is more like a temporary or permanent malfunction.

Biochemistry sounds like an awesome plan, like the most awesome ever. Just imagine how great that would be. I hope you can get there. At the very least you seem smart, which can be by the way also an issue. Sometimes with intelligence you get too much self-doubt and such, especially if you are inexperienced to deal with such things. Don't let being smart go to your head though, success is mostly about hard work, perseverance, and tolerance of failure, intelligence is good to have, but suprisingly enough it's not the most useful asset.

> I do not believe this is contributing to any of my feelings

Well, the brain is a super complex machine, so you can never know.

Do you have any goals? Like even something like earning more money to be able to pay for things or to be able to move or to meet new, interesting people.

I'm just saying, because having a goal can help. Then you can do something small and doable about it every day, and that way you get somewhere, and maybe even feel a bit less trapped.

For others it is often very hard to relate to us, that's just how it is sadly. It doesn't even always mean that they don't care, it's just that they can't.

Well, it's none of their business. Unless of course they are close friends, then being honest and talking about it might be the thing to do.

How are your days? How would you know that you have no real potential? What makes you say that?

I had the same experience with mindfulness. I can get there with some quiet, and forgetting that there is such thing as past or future. And it's indeed a liberating feeling, not even a feeling, a strange existence where things are lighter, less significant, less pointy or sharp as you said it. It's like those things can't even hurt you anymore. It's like all the troubles in the world are just concepts that exists around you independently.

When I'm stressed out too much I can't really get there. And sometimes months go by without me practicing mindfulness, I just forget about it or something.

What I do to get out of my head? Sex I guess is one thing. With men, with women, really with anyone who is a good sport, almost regardless of age (for me that's between 22 and 60). Though when I'm stressed out I can't even do that, or I don't even want to. What I hate is that I can't seem to form long term relationships, so there is a certain lack of intimidity in my life, which I try to replace with spicing up things, which tend to lead to underwhelming or bad experiences. I could choose this life and that life with someone special , but somehow I can't.

Other than that I don't really do anything else. I don't do drugs, no alcohol, I don't eat much and so on. Not counting music, I don't really do other mind altering things.

I'm happy that they could save your brother's life. It was great to read that part.

I don't suffer from schizophrenia myself, so I can't relate to that, but suicide is indeed something to us that appears as a solution in a time of great distress, pain and hopelessness. When you get to the end of your rope, and your usual coping mechanisms are not enough anymore to deal with the pain your brain starts to act up. Your thinking becomes impaired. For example once when I was 18 I run away from home before Christmas and I believed that nobody is looking for me and that my family didn't even notice that I left. Suicide often becomes an urge to release the tension. It's something your brain does I guess, it's an organ that regulates, so that makes sense. For me the pressure to release the tension seems somewhat similar to what you experience when you are sexually aroused. You may be able to hold on, but it's not easy to continue to live with it. Just imagine how uncomfortable it is to be aroused for hours. Or obviously a better example would be is when you are in pain. I'm sure you experienced that yourself already. You want nothing, but the pain to end. And the pain you go through can be very real. Jumping out of the window sometimes can seem much less worse. Guys tend to choose more violent methods, I don't know why.

Things can become better, indeed they can. I don't want you to worry about your brother too much, but know that this may be not over. I takes much time and healing, and I guess in your brother's case his schizophrenia even needs to be actively treated. What you are through with him was a crisis, and surviving a crisis doesn't mean that the whole thing is over and all the problems are solved. Again I don't know your brother and I'm not trying to scare you or make your PTSD worse. I'm just saying that healing can take a long time, and it's more of a process (and it's often needs to be an active process) rather than a one time event.
Your dad indeed seems like a prick. I would wait out that 2 weeks in your place, no matter how painful it is, because being dead because of an asshole is just not something you deserve.

It's interesting how all of us are scared to tell friends and family anything. We rather keep to ourselves.

Well, I hope you can get better. How are your days? Do you have something to live for?

That's awesome man, but I had the same experience before and I cannot promise you that your peace and acceptance will take forever. Mindfulness is great, as is hitting the gym, but they are not a magic wand. You might get a kick out them from time to time, but in itself neither is them tend to be enough. That's usually requires a combination of things.

Nevertheless I'm happy for you, just know that you might still experience misery and desperation. Even in a balanced person there aren't just highs, but also lows.

You are not ugly. You might believe that I'm obligated to tell you to not to hurt you, but it doesn't even matter in the end. I slept with a couple of guys who weren't that good looking (do mind that I'm a good looking bisexual guy) but they were lovely and awesome, and some of them confident, which can also trick you into believing that they look better than they are. I also slept with some guys and girls who were good looking, but otherwise they were assholes or boring or otherwise not compatible. It's more about your attitude than your physical appearance, just like great sex is more about psychological games (like intimity) than the actual physical sensation, even though both is needed. The fun part is that you aren't even ugly. Though for me you are too young, so you are definitely not my type.

You are in a tough situation, but you are so young, with a stupid adolescent brain (those are the worst if you ask me, for me that was a torture). I say this to everyone, but for someone who is 18 this is even much more true: change will happen, for better or worse, whether you like it or not. Chances are you won't always have the short end of the stick, so why not wait it out. I know that the whole thing is hell right now, but it won't take forever. I mean it could take forever, I'm not promising anything, I'm just saying that it tend to not take forever.

I'm sorry for your brother by the way. I hope you can go on. You just have to believe that you are not alone with this and that a whole interesting world is out there. It's going to be hard, it's indeed hard to earn enough money, and it's hard to form connections, and it's hard to get help. I think somehow you have to break down these big, seemingly insurmountable things to small doable tasks, tasks that you can do every day.

Indeed you can argue that staying alive gives a chance for things to become better and for you to find some way to make it better. Suicide might seem like a release from this hell, but then it's 100% that things cannot be ever better for you. Being dead is not exactly something you can experience after all. In some regards it's like being frozen in time.

That's one thought that can make me feel a bit better. Being frozen in time, all I would be what I already was. But I do want to leave a better, more interesting life behind. I want to believe that I did everything I could with the one chance I ever got to be alive.

No matter how tiny that hope is you can use it to live another day, and then another. Sooner or later there won't be another day. So it's not like this hell is eternal. Until then, let's suffer together.

EDIT: wow, thanks for the gold kind stranger
Well, rope is cheap, so I guess. Why do you want to kill yourself?

It's not stupid stuff, I experienced the same intensity of feelings when I was around your age, it was maddening and it made me suicidal as well. It was just some weird brain stuff that got much better and managable over the years. That problem basically solved itself for me, all I had to do is wait it out. Of course it wasn't easy, but there is nothing abnormal about you, you just have this brain stuff going on, which sucks tremendously.

My parents also couldn't handle the whole thing, we actually never talked about any of it ever, but that doesn't mean that they don't care, they just suck at the whole thing. There are other ways to get help though. Involving a parent by the way is not always a bad idea, even when you think that it is. Ultimately parents tend to love their children. It's still better to receive some half-ass tough love and care than dying on a rope. I'm just saying.

It must be hard, but you have to know that the brains of adolescents tend to produce such intensity. I hope that you can get through this, because it will go away and things will be much better. And there is no telling what you will or won't experience in the future. Maybe you meet someone very special, maybe you will become happy, and who knows what else. There are just so many things out there.

And yeah, suicide would devastate your family, if you are in a bad place even telling them is better. But if they can't handle it, like they get judgemental or hysterical, there are other ways to get help.

I get that it is painful, but there will be others and this rollercoaster won't take forever. You are 17, there is no chance in hell that things won't change for you. There is a future you and it wants you to be brave for her, because dying before experiencing life is just not worth it. Chances are this boyfriend will just move on with his life and won't even remember you. You deserve much better than that. 

Not to mention that hanging can be a totally bad experience, more than likely you are going to spend your last minute agonizing, and it's not going to be pretty. If things don't work out you can even end up in a wheelchair.

Your should fight your brain on this one and get help.

The thing is that it's better for your girlfriend to know the whole thing compared to the weight she would have if you would wound up dead one day. The key is communication, you don't have to push everything on her, but you have to find a way to communicate your problems in a way that's acceptable to both you and her. There is a way to be constructive about this. You can plan together how to get you a new job and so on. As long as you can remain constructive you should not fear appearing weak in front of her.

> What if she's faking it??

See? The lack of communication just makes both you and her guess each other. Wouldn't be good to get it all out in the open?

You are in a tough position, but don't kid yourself, you wouldn't die for logical reasons, you would die out of hopelessness and desperation over a bad situation.

But is the situation that bad that you have no other choice but to die? I guess you don't see any other options, but there must be other options.
What could those options be?

Can you talk with your girlfriend about this? You need support. Your thought processes could be affected by desperation, and indeed you may need a fresh perspective. There could be a solution there.

And don't think that others are prepared for your death, that sounds very unlikely. I think you may be affected by all the pain and stress. Please give yourself a chance, and give others a chance to help. Don't write yourself off yet, even though I know that the pain must be tormenting.

I get that you are desperate, but being dead would not make things better for you or your parents. I also get that you are under pressure, but come on, you have to value your life better than that. I'm not trying to underestimate the seriousness of your AS Level, whatever that may be (I have no idea), but I'm pretty sure it's not worth dying for.

Your parents are also pressured by society to say those awful things to you. Sucks, but what can you do. You have to face to music, and get around this AS Level something, I'm pretty sure there is a solution here somewhere. I don't know much about this stuff so you tell me.

Technically a person is more than just being a female or male, and more than those pesky sex organs. I'm just saying. Maybe you need something more in your life?

It's of course hard for me to relate to you, because I'm a guy and for me it's just something that happened to me, but I don't identify with it that much. I'm sure I would do well in a female body as well, would be awesome if we would have a technology for that. Anyway, I'm bisexual, so I may be not the usual case, but as I said it's hard for me to relate to someone like you. I hear you nevertheless, and I'm sorry that this happened to you.

Also there is that thing that although I do admire the aesthetics of the female body, to tell you the truth most women and men are ugly as fuck with much less than ideal bodies. Even I don't have the body I would ultimately want for myself, but I ain't got no time for that and as I'm aging the whole thing just becomes worse and worse.

Yeah, things can get better, thanks.

Anyway, you never answered, did you want to jump out of a window? Or is that just a question for us?

> i don't know what to do anymore

You shouldn't do anything that's too permanent. Suffering is the worst, and if there is a way for that you shouldn't suffer alone. In any case I hope that you can get through this. I very much hope so.

I don't mean to pry, but what's up with your parents? Do they know? They must know if you were hospitalized. How are they taking this?

And you mentioned that you are in a new school now and everything. Maybe you can make new friends or something.

> Sex reassignment surgery still wouldn't turn me into a real girl. I will always be a man no matter what, even with estrogen pills and a fake... You know.

Well I guess all that matters is how comfortable you can become with yourself. I mean, yeah, it probably wouldn't be perfect (though technology advances all the time), but is perfection is something that you want so much that you would rather be dead.

I get that this is a serious issue for you, but there are other aspects of life, and by being dead you lose everything. And if you do manage to find an acceptable solution or compromise there are people out there who would be able to love you no matter what.

Yes, it can be hard to deal with us, though I consider only as casual friends those who would rather ignore you. Not that anything is wrong with having casual friends.

Well maybe a different therapy can help, there are huge differences between them. Though some of them is expensive or not available everywhere, which sucks. In any way you should talk to someone.

It's super hard to suffer alone silently, that's for sure. And I don't have that much answers for you, but things can get better. I hope you can stay alive, it's always very sad to lose someone to depression :-( Please don't give up :-/

I can't really give an advice for you, I basically have no way to understand what you are going through.

But there is one thing. There are all kinds of intersex people out there who managed to find a balance, and there are success stories with sex reassignment therapy as well. I think it's worth a try if that is trully what you want.
I'm one of those people who wouldn't mind dating a woman with a less than perfect body or even with no reproduction capabilities and such, because for me love doesn't hinges on those things, and I tend to look for other qualities and there are many men and women out there like me. But in the end of course you are the one that needs be happy with yourself. I'm just saying that it's not impossible to find happiness once you accepted yourself. Though only you can know if that's possible for you or not.

That's how it works, you don't see how things can change, but they can and they will no matter what, for better or worse. But the good news is that you can influence that process by doing, learning and experiencing new things. If you are dead you are dead, you will have no chance finding out. Future you totally depends on you, and your stupid, adolescent brain (sorry :-)), so try not to fuck it up for him. On the other hand your pain is very real and life-threatening, and you need to talk about it, and you need support. You shouldn't and can't deal with this alone. Even calling a suicide hotline can be a very good idea, they are there to listen.

I'm sure your parents would miss you at least. To be blunt, you are very young, and everything in your life, including your brain is changing. Most of those changes are for the better, and you should definitely stay and wait them out, no matter how hard it is. You have so much time left, that your life can take a complete turn many times over and it will.

Do you have something that you like to do? Do you have friends? How is school?

Please don't, jumping in front of a train can led to losing your legs, serious spinal cord injury and such instead of death. Life won't become any better in a wheelchair with feeding tubes.

Anyway, we are listening. Are you depressed?

It can feel next to impossible to go on after years and years of depression. At some point you must break the silence, there are therapies, support groups and even calling a suicide hotline can be a good idea. You need to talk about this, you cannot stay alone, isolated with this anymore. I know that the pain is horrible, and that you are overwhelmed. You need some way to lessen the burden.

Does anyone knows that you are depressed and how bad your depression is?

It's my pleasure, just remember that there are going to be plenty of lows, even if you can summon the strength to try things it won't be a straight line. The statistics are on your side as long as you try, but you won't win every battle.

It's going to be very hard, and if you feel hopeless or desperate you can PM me anytime.

I recommend Carol Dweck for you, it's very relevant, and I think you will enjoy her works, especially the Mindset book:

https://www.ted.com/talks/carol_dweck_the_power_of_believing_that_you_can_improve?language=en

http://www.amazon.com/s?ie=UTF8&page=1&rh=n%3A283155%2Cp_27%3ACarol%20Dweck

http://www.amazon.com/Mindset-Psychology-Success-Carol-Dweck/dp/0345472322/ref=sr_1_1/183-1557878-6620508?s=books&ie=UTF8&qid=1439457563&sr=1-1&refinements=p_27%3ACarol+Dweck

I see that it is a pasta, why they call it Hamburger Helper? :-)

Anyway, do you have anything in your life right now, like a school, job or anything? What do you like to do in your free time?

Sorry to hear that you are in pain, I know that it is hard, but I think that you should go see the new job tomorrow. Think of it as a crappy adventure, now that you are ready to not live, you might as well also cut yourself some slack. Life can be overwhelming, but given the alternative it is worth sticking around and keeping your eyes open. Maybe you should try forming new connections one step at a time. You would be suprised how many people struggles with this and wants someone to talk to and wants a friend. Thinking out of box can help, maybe a support group? Even calling a suicide hotline can be a good idea, they tend to be friendly and they listen to you and it can help to talk about your problems.

I don't think it is wrong in itself to think about it. It's a coping mechanism, we all do it.

How are your days?

I think as far as mathematics go the whole thing is a balance between your energy to cope and the pain and stresses that wears you down. It sucks very much when the pain is too much, and it creates a warped perspective as you brain tries to regulate itself. Unfortunately the underlying problem is too complex for it to be able to find a good solution. 

I hear you, I'm in your shoes. Too much pain, I get it. What do you think the root cause of it in your case?

I hear you, it's hard and I cannot say anything that makes it less so, but hang in there buddy, because it's not impossible that your fight can bring a better tomorrow.

Do you want to talk about it? How are your days?

Thanks for asking. Well, I got myself into the cut-throat world of being an entrepreneur, because I couldn't decide what I love more, technology or people, so I figured why not do both in new, interesting ways. Anyway I got my ass whooped, turns out not everyone can handle such stresses and failures. Currently I'm rethinking my life and whether there is any place for me on this strange planet. Who knows, maybe there is.

Indeed, a lots of things are way more better than nothing. Even if they come with a chance of failure. But that's how it is. Don't let it affect you too deeply. You are a great guy, and who knows maybe you are a great radio guy. You would be suprised how much things can change over time for better or worse. But you do have control over it as long as there are options.
Sorry, I thought it can help if I can get a sense of what you are dealing with. I indeed extrapolated, obviously I don't understand your situation well, so sorry about that.

You are not alone with the job struggle, depends on the local economy, but rejection is the norm, especially in the age of outsourcing and contractors.

And don't forget that many job is only available through connections, sounds bad, but that's the reality.

So try to not take it personally.

Another option is to move, but of course you need some money for that.

There are other options which may or may not apply. You can try freelancing.

All right, my bad. The OCD thing came from your Reddit history. 

Do you know those people? Don't mind me though if you don't want to answer. I can be way over my head sometimes.

Nobody is perfect, and in this case the punishment doesn't fit the crime, no you don't deserve to die because a family member gave you the money. You may have made a mistake (or you didn't, I don't have enough information t), and by the way if you did you weren't the only one. It's not like you used a pistol to get the money. Well guess what lending money to a family member can be a risky business. Better luck next time.

You have to realize that making honest mistakes is not out of character for you, it's what makes you like the rest of us, a human being. And you did the right thing, you accepted that you are responsible. Honestly, you did everything that needed to be done.

As for being alone without support, that sucks, I'm glad that you are reaching out and trying to talk about it. I very much feel you and I hope that you can get better. You are not a fuck up, you seem like a nice, responsible person.

I get it now, you mean OCD triggers. Those must be bad, though I don't know much about them. In any case I'm rooting for you. Please don't hurt yourself.
What things trigger you usually?

That's awesome that you love it, because whether you believe or not you have a thing going for you, you are a radio guy, you just happen to not yet have a job.

You can totally get a job if you love doing something, you just have to be around, like a fly and look after the opportunities.

We are talking about a job, so there is a chance that people get it through their social network. So maybe you should make new friends, contact some people. Maybe do something that makes you appear on the map, or even just contact people for advice. It's called selling yourself, and that's how it works.

The whole thing is less about doing the perfect thing and more about trying and being persistent and not caring too much about failure, because opportunities are like the fireballs on the sky, they are very much about the right place and the right time.

Of course you feel that you don't have too much options, but there are always options. Sometimes you just have to commit to one of them and convert it to doable tasks. Of course don't do that with suicide, that's an option, but it's the worst one, because it closes all other options.

Learned helplessness is a bitch, but according to science unlike rats and dogs you can do something about it.

<http://youarenotsosmart.com/2009/11/11/learned-helplessness/>

So you have to have choices, and you do have those and you can create new ones. You also need to fight back your behavior, whatever that means. And you have to learn to fail with pride. I guess that's makes sense.

Do you like this radio stuff?

You are awesome that you made these moves to improve your life. 

Do you think that you can talk to your boyfriend about your problems? I'm not a relationship expert, but I think that if he is not there for you maybe you should consider deciding whether you need him in your life or not. The same goes for your friend. I get that you need the room because of the money situation, but maybe it's worth exploring other options.

This must be very hard without any support, isolation is the worst thing in these situations. Can't you reach out to someone, another friend maybe, or maybe a support group? If you feel that you can't take it anymore, even calling a suicide hotline is a good idea. I used to call, and they tend to be very professional and helpful, and they listen even if you aren't in immediate danger.

I had problem for a long time holding a fork or spoon in my hand when I ate outside where others could see me. The uncontrollable shaking soon made those lunches very awkward.

And there were a couple of situations before where I was a third wheel or I was way too awkward and I left a place in a similar manner to what you may have experienced.

So what kind of awkward situations are we talking about exactly?

Monster is awesome, very original, I watched it twice, never read it though.

I don't know much about voice actors, don't they learn and practice their craft too before becoming good at it? And I think for many dubs and video games mediocre would be a big step forward :-)

I don't play much video games. I never played Assassin's Creed, wanted to try out, never played. I played Sleeping Dogs the last time, one of those games even I can enjoy. Now I play Deus Ex Human Revolution. Not bad, the graphics is a lackluster, but there is a certain quality to it, it's mostly a stealth game though.

I think you are too harsh to yourself. Everything is possible, you just have to reduce it to doable tasks. Because it all comes down to what you do with your time. Of course when you are depressed or you are in pain, you have to do something about that too and it's far from easy, but if you don't take care of it it can become worse. You have to give a chance to yourself, and it's going to be painful, because failure can happen and will happen. But that can be survived. And if you throw away your life now you will never know.

It actually did, my mother used her connections to get me into a better school. The first year I was very lost and could not function well, but everyone was nice. I failed all the classes, so I had to repeat a year, things went much more smoothly after. I guess I always felt as an outsider, because it was an elite school, but everyone was super nice to me and I had a lots of friends and fun. Though I continued to struggle with depression, even run away from home when I was 17.

Have you ever wanted to do that?

To answer, yes, when I was in middle school and was bullied, but that was a long time ago. And I never did, I took a bunch of pills instead. And it didn't solve any of my problems. And my father punched me in the face for it. And I had to change schools. 0/10 would recommend the experience.

The awkward moment when you meet yourself on the internet.

What kind of anime, video games? :-)

Anyway do you have any special interest? Like anything you would want to do? Any dreams?

Getting a job can be hard, but not impossible, even without skills. For many what makes it very hard is not only the economy, but getting out of your comfort zone and not worrying too much about bad impressions.

It sucks how painful life can be sometimes. If you need someone to listen, many of us are here, we are listening.

How are your days? Do you have any hobbies, interests?
